mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original certificate issued by the Companies Office. For Hague-Apostille states, present the original or a notarized certified copy to the Department of Internal Affairs Authentications Unit for a New Zealand apostille. For non-Hague states, present the document to the Department of Internal Affairs for authentication, then lodge it at the consular section of the destination country's embassy or high commission in Wellington for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office, issued under section 214 of the Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original certificate or notarized copy. For Hague members, submit to the Department of Internal Affairs for apostille. For non-members, first obtain Department of Internal Affairs certification, then complete consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or high commission in Wellington. Never apply apostille and consular legalization as a successive chain; they are alternative routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (Certified Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of NZ_LTD as constituted by the founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified extract of the board resolution signed by the chairperson and company secretary, notarized by a New Zealand notary public. For Hague member destinations, the notarized document receives an apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs. For non-Hague destinations, the notarized document is authenticated by the Department of Internal Affairs and then submitted for consular legalization at the destination embassy or high commission in Wellington. Use only one route, never both in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: NZ_LTD as adopted by the incorporating shareholder in accordance with the Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registered articles or a notarized certified copy of the constitution. For Hague states, obtain a Department of Internal Affairs apostille. For non-Hague states, obtain Department of Internal Affairs certification followed by consular legalization before the document is used abroad. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; no document may undergo both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A fully licensed New Zealand bank or recognized licensed electronic money institution engaged for the historical account relationship, such as ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited, ASB Bank Limited, Bank of New Zealand, or Westpac New Zealand Limited
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original reference letter on bank letterhead signed by an authorized banking officer. The signature must be notarized. For Hague member states, attach a Department of Internal Affairs apostille. For non-Hague states, attach Department of Internal Affairs authentication and consular legalization from the destination embassy or high commission in Wellington. The apostille route and consular route are separate and must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: At incorporation and onboarding, the registered agent must screen all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners and key managers against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications, European Union consolidated financial sanctions, United Kingdom OFSI consolidated list, and New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions notices and designated terrorist entities under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002. PEP status must be established for senior political figures, family members and close associates, including domestic and foreign PEPs identified through publicly available registries, using a risk-based approach. Non-documentary verification, biometric identity, and electronic address verification are required; adverse media and politically exposed database screening must occur before issuance of any no-consent-to-carry-out-transaction decision.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register online portal operated by the New Zealand Companies Office at companiesoffice.govt.nz, including the Name Availability Search and online company name reservation function
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet or romanized te reo Maori transliteration. The Companies Act 1993 requires every limited company to include Limited or Ltd as the final word; Chinese characters or other non-Latin scripts are not permitted in the registered legal name. If a foreign-language trading name is desired, a romanized transliteration must be recorded and appended to the registered English name. The four-tier naming convention comprises the distinctive main name, the descriptive activity element, the legal form element, and any restricted-word consent conditions imposed by the Registrar or sector regulators.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a formal request for review with the Registrar of Companies via the Companies Office portal within 15 working days. The submission must set out why the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing reserved name, and why no statutory condition under sections 21 to 23 of the Companies Act 1993 has been breached. Premium surcharges or court proceedings are not required at first instance. If the Registrar issues a second refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 within 28 days. A professional legal opinion should accompany any request for approval of a prohibited token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used as the initial registered office only if it has a physical New Zealand street address capable of receiving court and registry documents; a private bag or PO box will be rejected. However, for ISIC 4791 TikTok Shop retail and social commerce, New Zealand banks and Inland Revenue will generally require a substantive physical trading or administrative presence, evidenced by lease or utility bill, before approving merchant settlement accounts and GST registration. Pure virtual-office addresses without personnel trigger enhanced customer due diligence and may be refused for Wise B2B and TikTok Shop payouts. Thus, a virtual office is acceptable for registry purposes but materially inadequate for banking onboarding and commercial substance validation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: presence of signage or staff; ability to produce lease or tenancy agreement; operating bank account statements referencing the premises; GST and tax filings identifying the physical location; and absence of domestic nexus fraud indicators such as mail-forwarding without personnel. For a low-risk online retail entity using short-video platforms, the probability of unannounced physical inspection by municipal inspectors or the Companies Office is low to moderate, estimated at 15 to 25 percent annually if anomalies such as virtual-only address, no staff, or multiple entities sharing the same address are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12, 16, 19, 22, 24, 25, 39, 40, 42, 44, 60, 61, 65, 110, 126, 151-154, 185-189 and 192; Companies (Registration) Regulations 2016; Companies (Availability of Names) Regulations 2014; Financial Reporting Act 2013 (if applicable for reporting entity status)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Business Registries, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), through the Companies Register online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Registration of a Company, submitted electronically via the New Zealand Companies Office online incorporation service under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up share capital and no blocked escrow or capital-impound account for a private limited company. The company may be incorporated with zero paid-up shares. Shares must be issued under section 39 and section 40 of the Companies Act 1993 for consideration in cash or money's worth as determined by the board. There is no legal requirement for non-resident shareholders to contribute local capital, and no parity value or statutory capital maintenance account is required for ordinary e-commerce activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS; SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION; REGISTERED OFFICE; BANKING AUTHORITY; AND STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, as a pro-forma first resolution of the board of directors of [COMPANY] (the Company), adopted in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution of the Company, as follows: 1. INCORPORATION AND CONSTITUTION. The board ratifies the incorporation of the Company by the Registrar of Companies and confirms that the constitution (if any) registered with the Companies Office is adopted as the Company's constitution. 2. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND CAPITAL. The board acknowledges that the initial subscribers have agreed to subscribe for the shares set out in the share register. The directors are authorized to issue shares at the consideration stated in the application and to receive funds in cash or money's worth. No share shall be treated as fully paid unless payment has been received in accordance with section 40 of the Companies Act 1993. The board directs the Company Secretary to record all issued shares in the share register. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE. The board approves the registered office of the Company located at [Registered Office Address, New Zealand] and directs the Company Secretary to file any change in the registered office with the Companies Office within ten working days. The address for service for the Company shall be [Address for Service] and remains designated for service of legal documents until amended by subsequent resolution. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The board authorizes the opening of bank and merchant accounts with [Name of Bank] for the conduct of TikTok Shop social commerce operations and payment settlement via TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B. The directors and authorized signatories listed in the bank mandate are authorized to sign, endorse, draw, settle, and manage electronic transfers, cheques, foreign exchange contracts, payout confirmations, and account statements. The bank is authorized to act on this mandate until written notice of revocation is received by the bank. 5. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The board appoints [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to hold office until the next annual shareholder meeting or until earlier removal, subject to applicable law and the Company's constitution. The Company Secretary is responsible for maintaining the company records, statutory registers, and regulatory filings. 6. GENERAL COUNSEL AUTHORIZATION. The board authorizes the Company Secretary and every solicitor engaged by the Company to file, execute, and deliver all statutory instruments, compliance returns, and regulatory notifications necessary to maintain the Company's good standing and to bind the Company in ordinary operational matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before incorporation, submit an electronic name availability check using the Companies Office online name search tool. Under sections 19 and 22 of the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar may refuse a name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, that suggests inappropriate connection with the Crown or a government agency, or that is prohibited under the Companies (Availability of Names) Regulations 2014. For a TikTok Shop e-commerce retail company, select a distinctive English-language word or invented name ending in Limited. Confirm the name does not mislead under the Fair Trading Act 1986. If the name contains restricted words or names of a living person, obtain prior written consents to attach to the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and up to three alternates
Written consent if the name includes a restricted word or living person's name
Name reservation fee confirmation if using a standalone reservation
Statement of the principal business purpose (e-commerce retail sales via short video platforms)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or refused, select an alternative non-conflicting name and resubmit; if the objection concerns trademark rights, obtain a written coexistence or consent letter from the objecting trademark owner or choose a new name before proceeding to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Electronic Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online incorporation service, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online application for incorporation under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993. Enter the approved company name, registered office street address in New Zealand (a post office box is not sufficient), address for service, full legal name and address of each director and shareholder, share classes and allotment schedule, and any optional constitution. Verify that each director satisfies the eligibility requirements under sections 151 to 153, including being a natural person aged at least 18, consenting in writing, and complying with the New Zealand resident-director requirement. Non-resident shareholders are permitted. Review the application carefully, then execute and submit it electronically. Pay the prescribed registration fee. Retain the electronic acknowledgment, transaction ID, and lodged application copy as proof of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic Form 1 application
Consent to act as director signed by each proposed director
Constitution document if the default Companies Act 1993 constitution is not adopted
Shareholder identification and share allocation schedule
Registered office address and address for service
Payment confirmation for the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice, access the query through the Companies Register portal, correct the affected fields, upload missing consents or documents, and resubmit within the Registrar's response period. If the application is suspended because a director consent is missing, obtain and file the required consent immediately and request reinstatement of the pending application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration, NZBN Issuance, and IRD Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies (New Zealand Companies Office) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar of Companies incorporates the company, issues a Certificate of Incorporation, a unique company number, and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The Companies Office automatically transmits registration data to the Inland Revenue Department for income tax registration. Inland Revenue will issue an IRD number and may issue a confirmation letter addressing any provisional tax, GST, or employer obligations. Obtain the official company extract from the Companies Register and download the NZBN certificate. Verify that the company legal name, registration date, registered office, directors, and shareholding records match the approved application. File the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN certificate, IRD acknowledgment, and company extract in the statutory corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Official Companies Office company extract
NZBN registration certificate
IRD number and tax registration acknowledgment
Incorporation application acknowledgment and receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NZBN or IRD number is not received within the expected service window, contact the Companies Office registration support desk and the Inland Revenue Business Registrations team with the assigned company number. If automatic IRD data transfer failed, complete the prescribed IRD online registration for the newly registered company using the NZBN as primary identifier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records Adoption, Bank Account Activation, and Tax Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors; New Zealand Companies Office; Inland Revenue Department; commercial banks and licensed payment service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and formally adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution covering share capital subscription, registered office retention, banking authorization, and appointments of officers. Minute the resolution and place it in the company's minute book. Open a business bank account or a licensed non-bank payment account using the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, company extract, director identification, and banking authority resolution. Register the company for Goods and Services Tax with Inland Revenue if the TikTok Shop retail turnover will or does exceed the NZD 60,000 threshold in any twelve-month period. Complete bank customer due diligence, confirm the specified payment rails of TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B, and document the beneficial ownership chain and source of funds for TikTok Shop payouts. Update the Companies Office if any officer details change after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed pro-forma first board resolution
Bank or payment service provider account application
Certificate of Incorporation and official company extract
Passport or government-issued ID of each director and beneficial owner
Proof of address for each director
NZBN letter and IRD number acknowledgment
TikTok Shop seller registration and payout routing information
Wise B2B account authorization form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application, provide a full corporate ownership chart, source-of-wealth documents, and, if necessary, arrange a video interview or an in-person visit to satisfy enhanced due diligence. If the payment service provider requires a longer review, apply simultaneously to an alternative licenced bank or non-bank payment provider while maintaining compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are undertaken under ISIC 4791. The registered activity is pure social-commerce retail through the TikTok Shop platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no industrial operating permit is required for ISIC 4791. The company must only comply with ordinary business registration requirements under the Companies Act 1993, tax registration with Inland Revenue, and applicable consumer and e-commerce rules under the Fair Trading Act 1986 and the Consumer Guarantees Act 1993.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — Exempt from Environmental Impact Assessment requirements under the Resource Management Act 1991 because the activity involves no land-use change, no industrial facility, no chemical process, and no wastewater or emission-generating operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no point-source discharge of wastewater or process effluent, no volatile organic compound emissions, and no hazardous waste generation arise from TikTok Shop online retailing. If the company later uses a third-party fulfillment warehouse, the warehouse operator must separately maintain compliance with local council trade waste bylaws, stormwater permits, and any resource consents required under the Resource Management Act 1991.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — the activity does not involve a physical premises requiring Civil Defence fire permits, structural load inspections, or industrial workplace approvals. General workplace health and safety duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 apply to office and administrative workers. If a third-party logistics warehouse is used for TikTok Shop order fulfillment, that warehouse operator is independently responsible for fire safety certification, evacuation plans, hazardous goods storage approvals, and occupational workplace licences.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; electronic filing and registration through the myIR secure online portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity with a New Zealand tax nexus, whether deriving New Zealand-source income, carrying on a taxable activity, or making supplies subject to New Zealand GST, must obtain an IRD number from Inland Revenue. The entity must submit its statutory registration application through the myIR portal or by lodging the prescribed paper application with Inland Revenue, accompanied by foreign incorporation documents, certificate of good standing or equivalent, registered office and head office addresses, director and substantial shareholder details, the entity's foreign tax identification number, and a statement of the New Zealand activities giving rise to the tax nexus. Inland Revenue validates the identity and activity details and issues the IRD number, which serves as the single tax identification number for income tax, GST, payroll, and all other tax obligations. If the foreign entity incurs taxable supplies in New Zealand and is required to register for GST, the same IRD number is used as the GST/VAT registration number; no separate VAT identifier is issued. Entities that merely export goods from New Zealand without making taxable supplies in New Zealand may still voluntarily register for GST to claim input tax credits and substantiate zero-rating, subject to Inland Revenue approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in New Zealand. An eligible closely held company may elect look-through company (LTC) status, under which taxable income and losses flow through to shareholders. Hybrid and branch mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act 2007 (subpart FH) operate as mandatory statutory overrides rather than elective regimes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period; non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers are also required to register when their supplies to New Zealand exceed NZD 60,000 in the same period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based per-invoice stamping, or anti-fraud digital sealing. Tax invoices may be issued in electronic form if they contain all compulsory GST information under the GST Act 1985. Peppol e-invoicing is optional and supported by Inland Revenue. GST-registered persons file GST returns electronically through myIR, but there is no per-transaction government clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the GST Act 1985, a supply of goods qualifies for the zero rate when the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand in the course of the supply, the goods are not supplied for consumption in New Zealand, and the supplier retains conclusive evidence of physical export such as customs-approved shipping documentation. Services supplied by a New Zealand supplier to a non-resident customer may qualify for zero-rating if the services are performed or enjoyed outside New Zealand and are not connected with New Zealand land or moveable property. For TikTok Shop cross-border retail transactions, the New Zealand seller must demonstrate that the goods were sold and dispatched to a foreign customer, left New Zealand under customs supervision, and that export proceeds were received from outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Entry lodged through the Trade Single Window)
Commercial invoice and packing list evidencing the overseas buyer and consignee
Bill of Lading or air waybill showing export from New Zealand to a foreign destination
Cargo and shipping documentation confirming customs exit from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank-issued foreign exchange receipt showing receipt of the overseas buyer's payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit export supply records and require the complete customs and foreign-exchange documentation bundle before accepting the zero rate. If zero-rating is not substantiated, the supply is reassessed to GST at 15%, with use-of-money interest running from the original returns date. The Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes shortfall penalties for evasion or lack of reasonable care, including penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall for fraudulent or intentional withholding, and criminal sanctions may apply. Any GST refund claimed on the basis of unverified or false export documentation is retrospectively clawed back and assessed as ordinary taxable supply output, subject to the ordinary reassessment time bar unless fraud or misrepresentation is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a liberalised, fully convertible currency regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) floats freely, and there are no foreign exchange controls, surrender requirements, or central bank approval gates on either current account or capital account flows. The current account is fully convertible: trade payments, service fees, royalties, interest and dividends may be remitted without Reserve Bank of New Zealand or Inland Revenue consent, subject only to non-resident withholding tax and anti-money laundering verification. The capital account is likewise unrestricted for ordinary commercial equity and debt, although the Overseas Investment Act 2005 creates consent thresholds for sensitive land, significant business assets, fishing quota, or media licences, and those must be screened before the transaction is settled. Profit remittance is blocked only by standard corporate law duties and the bank's KYC verification of a valid board resolution, distributable reserves, and the absence of liquidity concerns. There is no exchange-control licensing system, no import/export FX allocation, no requirement to channel conversions through official windows, and no differentiation between residents and non-residents for access to FX products. Surplus NZD may be invested abroad or converted to any major currency at resident banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender regime: exporters may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts without compulsory conversion, and no mandatory conversion ratio or surrender timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / Capital Escrow Sweep Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Capital Escrow Sweep Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Capital Escrow Sweep Account
Multi-Currency Operational Account / Inbound Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs that are not registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register and are not reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 have low and practically unusable viability: they cannot lawfully open a New Zealand corporate account or operate settlement rails for the entity. Onshore or registered EMIs, in particular Wise B2B when appointed as the TikTok Shop payout rail, are feasible as a secondary, high-frequency collection rail, but they are not a substitute for a Tier-1 commercial bank because they generally lack documentary credit capacity, full Reserve Bank settlement access, and committed debt facilities. The prudent treasury structure is to use Wise B2B solely for platform payout capture and sweep every balance nightly to the Tier-1 bank, preventing aggregate exposure at any unbanked EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement exists under New Zealand corporate law for all directors to appear physically in-branch. Remote video onboarding is accepted by Tier-1 banks for New Zealand-registered companies, provided the company has a valid New Zealand registered office and maintains the statutory corporate administration obligations under the Companies Act 1993. Overseas directors may complete identity verification remotely using the bank's digital identity portal, or through consular notarisation/apostille where a proxy or authorised signatory attends a filmed interview. The bank may still require an in-person or recorded interview with any statutory director, beneficial owner, or treasury signatory who is assessed as high risk, and will require the original or certified copy of the board resolution authorising account opening and signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholding or undisclosed trust controller behind the NZ Ltd.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current and historical Companies Office extracts; statutory register of members; signed declaration of beneficial ownership; certified copy of any relevant overseas trust deed and trustee register; corporate law opinion identifying every individual with 25% or greater economic interest; and an independent background search on each ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented TikTok Shop payout flows through multiple aggregators, creating a commingling/invoice-verification red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution copy of the TikTok Shop seller agreement; 12 months of platform settlement statements with payout IDs and merchant reference numbers; sworn reconciliation prepared by an NZ chartered accountant; IRD GST and income tax filing certificates; supplier invoices and order history matching settlement values; and a written undertaking that the account will not be used for unrelated third-party receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or beneficial owner located in or connected to a FATF-monitored restricted jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified passport and proof of residential address; apostilled/consular 10-year police clearance; tax residence certificate from the country of residence; personal bank reference confirming source of funds for the preceding 36 months; employment and net-worth declarations; and an enhanced due-diligence questionnaire with recorded remote KYC interview and independent negative-media search.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection inconsistent with the stated TikTok Shop inventory funding plan, particularly when sourced from another EMI wallet.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed board resolution for capital raising and share allotment; bank capital-verification documents delivered to the bank; source-of-funds confirmation from the originating EMI or bank with the full SWIFT chain; notarised share subscription agreement; detailed 12-month business plan and inventory purchase contracts; proof that the remitting party is a true investor or related creditor; and tax clearance evidence from the remitter's jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial equity injection, remitters will send a SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment to the NZ entity's Tier-1 bank account. The payment purpose narrative must unambiguously state 'INWARD DIRECT INVESTMENT - EQUITY - SHARE SUBSCRIPTION - COMPANIES ACT 1993', and the remitter's bank should tag the transfer in the applicable international banking statistical field as overseas direct investment into New Zealand equity capital. Because New Zealand has no exchange controls, no Reserve Bank pre-approval or FX licence is required. The receiving bank performs the bank-side capital verification by obtaining a certified board allotment resolution, a share certificate issued to the investor, and confirmation that the cleared funds match the transaction amount. If the wire is in USD or another foreign currency, the receiving Tier-1 bank converts at the same-day spot rate; there is no forced conversion or custody requirement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border supplier and carrier disbursements should be made through SWIFT MT103 payments with full remittance details for amounts under the bank's high-value cap. Higher-risk or large-value consignments should be financed through irrevocable commercial documentary letters of credit governed by UCP600, and established trading partners may use documentary collections under URC522. Domestic NZD liquidity uses Payments New Zealand's Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) and the Reserve Bank real-time wholesale settlement, but these do not replace SWIFT for cross-border settlement. TikTok Shop operational disbursements and platform expenses can be handled through the registered EMI/Wise B2B rail with daily sweeping to the Tier-1 corporate account and full reconciliation against platform statements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward contracts in major crosses such as NZD/USD, NZD/CNH, NZD/AUD and NZD/EUR under ISDA/IFEMA master agreements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies that are subject to deliverability restrictions in the offshore market, such as IDR, VND and certain CNH counterparty limits; NZD settlement remains freely deliverable and cannot itself be forced into an NDF
Cross-currency swaps to hedge balance-sheet mismatches arising from funded inventory and medium-term platform supplier credit
Vanilla FX options, collars and zero-cost structures as an alternative to forwards, subject to the bank's counterparty credit and margin policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after the anniversary of the company's date of incorporation; if the anniversary falls at year-end, the return window runs in the next calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Companies Office issues an overdue/annual return reminder; after 12 months of non-filing, the Registrar may formally notify the company and directors and propose removal from the Companies Register under section 210. If no compliance or successful objection is made within the statutory response window, the company is administratively struck off and dissolved. Directors may also be prosecuted under the Companies Act, and restoration requires a court order or Registrar relief plus prescribed fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) under Income Tax Act 2007
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the balance date; where the company uses an approved tax agent, the deadline is automatically extended to 31 March of the following income year unless IRD applies an earlier date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers IRD's statutory late filing penalty (LFP) of NZ$250 plus NZ$50 for each subsequent 30-day non-compliant period, capped at NZ$1,000; use-of-money interest (UOMI) is charged on any terminal tax due from the original due date until payment at the IRD prescribed underpayment rate; persistent non-filing can lead to IRD assessment by default, debt enforcement, and prosecutions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax Return (GST-101) under Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For monthly and two-monthly taxable periods, the GST return is due on the 28th day of the month following the end of the taxable period; six-monthly GST filers file within one month after the end of that six-month period. A TikTok Shop retail entity normally files on the standard cycle determined by forecast GST turnover.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: IRD may impose a late filing penalty of NZ$250 plus NZ$50 for every 30-day period the GST return remains outstanding (for non-nil returns), along with use-of-money interest on any GST payable; continued default may subject the company to IRD collection action including government assessment and compulsory enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Large-Company Financial Statements Filing (Financial Reporting Act 2013 / Companies Act 1993)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the entity is required to file audited financial statements, they must be delivered to the Registrar within 6 months after the end of the accounting period; for a 31 March balance date this means no later than 30 September of the same year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file financial statements may result in Financial Reporting Act 2013 penalties (fine up to NZ$10,000 per officer on conviction), a Companies Office overdue notice, and repeated non-compliance can justify removal from the Companies Register. Directors are personally liable for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit by a Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ) certified auditor is mandatory if the company is 'large': total assets exceed NZ$60 million at balance date, or total turnover exceeds NZ$30 million, or it employs 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees, with the large test met where any two of the three indicators are exceeded. An audit is also compulsory if the company is an FMC reporting entity, if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares require an audit under the Companies Act, or if a court order or regulatory condition requires audited financial statements. Smaller companies that do not meet these tests are exempt from statutory audit unless shareholders or third-party users contractually require one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For large and publicly accountable entities, the governing framework is New Zealand IFRS (NZ IFRS), which incorporates IFRS as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board without significant modification. Non-publicly-accountable for-profit entities may elect NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); small and medium private companies may prepare special-purpose financial statements in accordance with Companies Act 1993 accrual accounting principles, subject to any shareholder or financial covenants requiring general purpose NZ GAAP or SME accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate stand-alone UBO filing under ordinary company law. Instead the Companies Act requires the company's own share register to be kept continuously current, and the annual return filed with the Companies Office must confirm the registered directors and shareholders. Any new share allotment must be reported to the Companies Office by a Return of Allotment within 10 working days. There is no 30-day UBO disclosure window; however, the AML/CFT Act 2009 requires corporate service providers and financial institutions that provide services to the company to verify and refresh beneficial ownership information, and the company must cooperate by providing its register within a reasonable time. All member transfers must be entered in the share register immediately and any resulting director/shareholder change reflected in the next annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250 - US$700 per annum for a compliant registered office and professional corporate secretarial agent; inclusive of annual return preparation and register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 if no statutory audit threshold is met; a voluntary certified audit for a small TikTok Shop retail entity of modest turnover typically costs US$3,500 - US$10,000 depending on transaction volume and group structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand companies are subject to a flat 28% corporate income tax rate. There is no generic patent box and no preferential free-zone corporate tax regime; the main effective incentives are the 15% Research and Development Tax Incentive for eligible R&D expenditure, the imputation credit system to mitigate economic double taxation of distributed profits, and the absence of a separate capital gains tax for most TikTok Shop inventory sales. Start-ups and innovative retailers may access the R&D credit, but social commerce income itself enjoys no sector-specific holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed through Inland Revenue myIR and the IRD e-filing portal; associated provisional tax and NRWT filings are made through IR6/IR67 as applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with provisional tax instalments during the income year and NRWT returns as payments are made to non-residents)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed and terminal tax paid by 7 July. For non-standard balance dates, the return is due on the 7th day of the fourth month after the balance date; tax agent extension arrangements may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable receipts from TikTok Shop sales, short-video live commerce, product sales, and marketplace facilitation revenues, stated in New Zealand dollars and net of GST and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A New Zealand-incorporated company is tax resident and must report worldwide income. TikTok Shop payouts routed through Wise or other payment rails must be converted using Inland Revenue foreign exchange indicator rates. A non-resident enterprise with no New Zealand permanent establishment would only report New Zealand-source income, but once the NZ Ltd is the contracting merchant, the full merchant margin is assessable in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: cost of goods sold, fulfilment and freight, TikTok Shop commissions, payment processing fees, live-stream production, influencer remuneration, platform advertising, returns provisions, and general overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must satisfy the general permission and apportionment rules of the Income Tax Act 2007. Payments to related non-resident suppliers, influencers, or group service companies are deductible only to the extent they are at arm's length and the payer has complied with NRWT or an approved treaty-relief procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or tax loss computed as gross assessable income less deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a loss arises, the loss carry-forward is subject to shareholder continuity requirements; a change in non-resident beneficial ownership of more than 51% will extinguish the loss. The Commissioner can disallow artificial losses created through mispriced TikTok Shop-related service recharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward and used in the current year, together with imputation credit account reconciliation data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a NZ Ltd with non-resident shareholders, imputation credits attached to dividends reduce only resident shareholders' income tax; they do not reduce the payor's obligation to deduct non-resident withholding tax from distributions. Benchmark dividends and imputation ratios must be monitored to avoid further dividend withholding payment liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax declarations: gross dividends, interest, and royalties paid or credited to non-residents during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all outbound profit repatriations through the IR4 supporting schedules. Statutory NRWT must be accounted for and remitted via the NRWT return. If a double tax agreement rate is claimed, retain the non-resident's valid Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership evidence, and the completed Inland Revenue rate declaration before the distribution is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable reconciliation: 28% corporate income tax on net taxable income, reduced by imputation credits, resident withholding tax credits, provisional tax payments, R&D tax credits, and other allowable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ Ltd cannot offset its corporate tax liability against NRWT owed on behalf of non-resident shareholders. Any DTA credit for foreign underlying tax must be substantiated separately; the company should reconcile IR6 provisional tax to the IR4 final liability to avoid use-of-money interest and late payment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and additional disclosure items: related-party transaction schedule, master file/local file notification, country-by-country reporting notification, and tax agent declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed the NZD 10 million Local File threshold, the entity must have contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation available. Groups with NZD 1.125 billion or more consolidated revenue must notify Inland Revenue and file CbCR schedules. Failing to disclose related-party arrangements involving TikTok Shop group entities materially increases shortfall penalty exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers a late filing penalty of NZD 250 under section 139A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus additional monthly late filing penalties until the return is filed. Late payment triggers an initial late payment penalty of 1%, a further 4% assessment penalty after seven days, and an ongoing 1% per month or part-month, together with use-of-money interest. Wilful evasion or fraudulent suppression of TikTok Shop revenue is a criminal offence under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 punishable by fines of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, in addition to civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax underpaid.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral double tax agreement relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must provide the NZ paying entity with a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent authority of the residence state, complete the Inland Revenue non-resident withholding tax rate declaration (typically via myIR using forms equivalent to IR1031), and provide documentary evidence of beneficial ownership showing the recipient is not a mere nominee or conduit. The NZ payer must not apply the reduced treaty rate until the reduced rate notification is approved; otherwise it remains liable for the full 30% NRWT. Records of all DTA claims, TRCs, ownership structures, and payment details must be retained for seven years. If excessive NRWT was withheld, the non-resident may file a claim with Inland Revenue for a refund on the basis of the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding tax on interest is 15% and on royalties is 15%. The Approved Issuer Levy can replace NRWT on interest paid by an approved NZ borrower to an unrelated non-resident lender at a concessional 2% rate where the statutory conditions are met. Under many of New Zealand's bilateral DTAs, interest withholding is reduced to 10% and royalties to 5% or 10%, depending on the nature of the rights and the beneficial ownership of the income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate cross-border related-party controlled transactions triggers the expectation of a contemporaneous transfer pricing Local File; Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting obligations arise for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of NZD 1.125 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations code comparable to low-tax offshore regimes, but economic substance is integral to the permanent establishment and transfer pricing rules. A TikTok Shop retail operation claiming to be a fully functioning NZ principal must demonstrate that the core income-generating activities, such as strategic inventory management, sales risk, platform contract negotiation, and customer-facing decision-making, are actually performed in New Zealand. Where the NZ entity is a shell that merely book-keeps live-commerce profits generated by foreign principals, the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the reconstruction powers in the transfer pricing rules enable Inland Revenue to re-attribute the profits to the substance-locating jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Unreported Offshore Receipts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing TikTok Shop payouts to a foreign Wise B2B or offshore bank account, deliberately omitting those gross receipts from the NZ Ltd's accounting system and IR4 return, and failing to remit the resulting corporate income tax and GST.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 criminalize evasion and the carrying on of business with intent to defraud, with fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years. The civil shortfall penalty for evasion is up to 150% of the tax underpaid under section 141D, plus use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or participate in the concealment are treated as aiding and abetting tax evasion. The corporate veil is pierced under the fraudulent trading provisions of the Companies Act 1993, making directors personally liable for the unpaid tax and creditors' losses. Inland Revenue may also issue a departure prohibition order under section 157 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, imposing an effective travel ban, and criminal conviction can lead to asset restraint and confiscation under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Substance Mismatch
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the TikTok Shop commerce chain so that the NZ Ltd earns a residual service fee while a related low-tax or no-tax platform entity receives 90% of the social-commerce profits without performing the actual live-streaming sales, inventory, or customer-risk functions, and failing to prepare a Local File despite related-party transactions exceeding the NZD 10 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections GC 1 and GC 6 of the Income Tax Act 2007 empower the Commissioner to reconstruct income using the arm's length principle. A transfer pricing shortfall penalty under section 141EB and an abusive tax position penalty under section 141E can be imposed at up to 50% of the resulting tax shortfall, with use-of-money interest; the documentation failure itself can lead to adverse inferences and evidentiary penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement the mispricing or fail to ensure the company's tax obligations are satisfied may be personally liable under section 149 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 for the company's tax liabilities. A breach of the directors' duties of care and good faith under sections 131 and 135 of the Companies Act 1993 exposes directors to compensation orders and restoration of diverted profits. Directors leaving New Zealand while such liabilities are outstanding may be subject to departure prohibition and arrest on departure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Unlawful Dividend Distributions Through Shell Entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident BVI, Seychelles, or similar shell company that is not the beneficial owner of the TikTok Shop retail profits, deliberately failing to withhold the 30% statutory NRWT, and declaring the distribution without satisfying the solvency test or while the NZ Ltd holds no distributable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section RA 7 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes the withholding obligation; section 139B applies penalty tax for failure to comply; section 141D can impose a 150% evasion penalty. Sections 52, 55, and 56 of the Companies Act 1993 render unlawful any dividend paid other than out of profits and after the solvency test, and impose personal recovery obligations on directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Companies Act 1993 requires directors who sign or authorize an unlawful dividend to repay the full amount with interest, and this obligation survives the company's liquidation. Inland Revenue can invoke section 149 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 to recover unpaid NRWT directly from directors. Non-resident directors face a departure prohibition order and, where fraud is proven, criminal prosecution for evasion with imprisonment up to five years and confiscation of assets derived from the unlawful repatriation.
